title: Joshua Commissioned to Lead
summary: After Moses's death, the LORD commissions Joshua to lead Israel across the Jordan, promising to be with him as with Moses; Joshua prepares the people, and the Transjordan tribes pledge their support.
blurb: The LORD commissions Joshua after Moses's death

title: Rahab and the Spies
summary: Joshua sends two spies to scout Jericho, and Rahab hides them from the king's men on her roof, securing a promise that she and her family will be spared when the city falls.
blurb: Rahab hides Israel's spies in Jericho

title: Crossing the Jordan
summary: As the priests carrying the ark step into the flooded Jordan, its water is cut off upstream, and all Israel crosses the riverbed on dry ground into the promised land.
blurb: Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground

title: The Memorial Stones at Gilgal
summary: Twelve men each carry a stone from the Jordan's dry riverbed, and Joshua sets them up at Gilgal as a memorial for future generations, then the river returns to its flood.
blurb: Twelve stones are set up at Gilgal

title: Circumcision, Passover, and the LORD's Commander
summary: Israel's new generation is circumcised and keeps the Passover at Gilgal, the manna stops the next day, and Joshua meets a mysterious commander of the LORD's army near Jericho.
blurb: Israel is circumcised and keeps the Passover

title: The Fall of Jericho
summary: Israel marches silently around Jericho once a day for six days, then seven times on the seventh; when the priests' trumpets sound and the people shout, the walls collapse and the city falls.
blurb: Jericho's walls fall after Israel marches around it

title: Achan's Sin and Defeat at Ai
summary: Achan secretly keeps devoted plunder from Jericho, and Israel is routed at Ai as a result; Joshua identifies the guilty man by lot, and Achan is executed with his family and plunder.
blurb: Achan's theft brings defeat, then his execution

title: Ai Falls and the Law Is Read
summary: Joshua captures Ai using an ambush after a feigned retreat, burning the city and killing its king, then builds an altar on Mount Ebal and reads the whole law to Israel.
blurb: Ai falls by ambush; the law is read

title: The Gibeonites' Deception
summary: Pretending to be travelers from a distant land, the Gibeonites trick Israel's leaders into a peace treaty; once exposed, they are spared because of the oath but made servants for the community.
blurb: The Gibeonites trick Israel into a treaty

title: The Sun Stands Still
summary: Five kings besiege Gibeon for making peace with Israel, Joshua marches all night to defend it, the LORD sends hailstones and stops the sun and moon, and the captured kings are executed at Makkedah.
blurb: The sun stands still over the battle

title: The Northern Campaign
summary: Jabin, king of Hazor, gathers a large coalition with horses and chariots at the waters of Merom, but Israel defeats them there and burns Hazor, the only northern city it sets on fire.
blurb: Jabin's northern coalition falls; Hazor is burned

title: The Defeated Kings
summary: The book tallies every king defeated in the conquest so far: two east of the Jordan under Moses and thirty-one west of it under Joshua, thirty-three kings in all.
blurb: Every defeated king is listed and counted

title: The Land Still to Be Conquered
summary: With Joshua now old and territory still unconquered, the LORD tells him to divide it among the tribes anyway, beginning with the land Moses already assigned east of the Jordan.
blurb: Unconquered land is divided among the tribes

title: Caleb's Inheritance
summary: At eighty-five, Caleb reminds Joshua of his faithful report as one of the twelve spies decades earlier and asks for the hill country of Hebron, which Joshua grants him.
blurb: Caleb asks for and receives Hebron

title: Judah's Territory
summary: Judah's borders and towns are recorded in detail as the largest tribal allotment, and within it Caleb's daughter Achsah marries Othniel after he captures Kiriath-sepher, then asks her father for springs.
blurb: Othniel wins Achsah by capturing a city

title: Ephraim's Territory
summary: Ephraim receives its allotted hill-country territory within the larger portion shared with Manasseh, but the tribe fails to drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, who remain as forced laborers.
blurb: Ephraim's territory keeps Canaanites in Gezer

title: Manasseh's Territory and Zelophehad's Daughters
summary: Manasseh's western territory is recorded, and Zelophehad's five daughters come forward to receive a land inheritance among their father's brothers since he had no sons, as the LORD commanded Moses.
blurb: Zelophehad's daughters receive their own inheritance

title: The Tabernacle at Shiloh and Benjamin's Territory
summary: Israel sets up the tabernacle at Shiloh and surveys the land still undivided among seven tribes; Benjamin, first to receive its portion, is given a narrow territory between Judah and Joseph including Jerusalem.
blurb: Benjamin receives land between Judah and Joseph

title: The Last Tribal Allotments
summary: The remaining seven tribes, including Simeon, Zebulun, and Dan, receive their territories by lot, and Israel finally gives Joshua the town he asked for, Timnath-serah in Ephraim's hill country.
blurb: Joshua receives Timnath-serah as his inheritance

title: Cities of Refuge
summary: Joshua designates six cities across the land, three on each side of the Jordan, as places where anyone who kills a person by accident can flee for protection from revenge.
blurb: Six cities of refuge are set apart

title: Levitical Cities and Israel's Rest
summary: The Levites receive forty-eight cities with pasturelands out of the other tribes' territory, and the chapter closes declaring that the LORD gave Israel all he promised and rest on every side.
blurb: The Levites receive forty-eight cities

title: The Witness Altar
summary: The Transjordan tribes head home and build a large altar by the Jordan; fearing rebellion, the rest of Israel prepares for war until Phinehas's delegation learns the altar is only a witness.
blurb: An altar by the Jordan nearly starts a war

title: Joshua's Farewell Warning
summary: Now old, Joshua gathers Israel's leaders one last time to warn them against intermarrying with the remaining nations or serving their gods, reminding them of the LORD's faithfulness in every battle.
blurb: Joshua warns Israel's leaders one last time

title: Covenant Renewal at Shechem
summary: At Shechem, Joshua recounts Israel's whole history and challenges the people to choose whom they will serve; they renew the covenant, and Joshua dies and is buried at Timnath-serah.
blurb: Choose this day whom you will serve
